title: Exact inverse image preserves K-flat resolutions
statement: Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. There exists an additive functor $I:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(g^{-1}\mathcal O_S)$ whose objects and maps are the canonical module inverse images [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]. This functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits. For every quasi-isomorphism $s:P^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] with $P^\bullet$ K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], the termwise map $I(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $I(P^\bullet)$ is K-flat over $g^{-1}\mathcal O_S$.

proof.text: Choose the canonical inverse-image module functor supplied by lem-pc-inverse-image-module-functor-exact. Its object and map formulas are definitional. Its additivity and finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation provide the first clauses.

For a K-flat resolution s, install its quasi-isomorphism clause as a local instance. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology gives that the image of s is a quasi-isomorphism, since an additive functor preserving finite limits and colimits preserves homology.

Use the ringed-space map with target ring sheaf the canonical inverse-image ring and structure morphism the inverse-image adjunction unit. Apply lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation to the K-flat source complex. The proved comparison lem-pc-inverse-image-tensor-pullback-comparison identifies this tensor pullback with the termwise inverse image.

K-flatness is invariant under an isomorphism of complexes: for an arbitrary acyclic test complex, map the isomorphism through the total-tensor bifunctor, and transport exactness in every degree using HomologicalComplex.ExactAt.of_iso. Combine this K-flatness with the quasi-isomorphism from step 2 to obtain the image K-flat resolution.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof of the existing route; exactness uses the Mathlib site-pullback and reflective sheafification argument instead of the stalk criterion. Identity tensor comparison is proved explicitly.

lean.statement: theorem exists_inverseImage_exact_kFlat {T S : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) : ∃ (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology T) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing g.base S.sheaf))) (hI : ∀ M, I.obj M = TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule g.base S.sheaf M) (_ : ∀ {M N} (a : M ⟶ N), I.map a = eqToHom (hI M) ≫ TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModuleMap g.base S.sheaf M a ≫ eqToHom (hI N).symm) (_ : I.Additive), PreservesFiniteLimits I ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits I ∧ (∀ {P G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) ℤ} (s : P ⟶ G), CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := S.sheaf) s → CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing g.base S.sheaf) ((I.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map s))
